source.title: On the Inconsistency of Kernel Ridgeless Regression in Fixed Dimensions
source.authors: Daniel Beaglehole; Mikhail Belkin; Parthe Pandit

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies inconsistency of fixed-dimensional kernel interpolation, but does not test the double-descent curves or the versions’ specified size, epoch, sample-size, or effective-complexity predictions. Double-descent results in related work are cited, not reproduced.
record.gate_note: Recorded the paper’s own fixed-dimensional inconsistency theorems and its expected-error-versus-bandwidth plot as related findings, not as tests of the specified claim versions. The double-descent results mentioned in related work are from other studies and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves fixed-dimensional inconsistency of translation-invariant kernel ridgeless regression and plots exact expected error over kernel bandwidth. It reports no test-error curve across an interpolation threshold over model size, epochs or sample count. Double-descent results appear only in cited related work ([18] random features). Its own results do not bear on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct, with one addition. The authors also say the result suggests infinitely wide neural networks (NTK) are inconsistent in fixed dimension. They also say high dimension dissipates the noise error.
record.recipe_differences: This is a fixed-design theoretical analysis of kernel interpolation using Fourier decompositions and expected-MSE bounds, with a bandwidth experiment; it does not reproduce double-descent sweeps over model size, training time, or sample size.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports a bandwidth trade-off: smaller bandwidth reduces noisy estimation error but worsens approximation error; larger bandwidth does the reverse. Its stated optimal bandwidth in the Figure 6.1b experiment is roughly M/N = 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated spectral assumptions, kernel ridgeless regression with translation-invariant kernels in fixed dimension has expected test MSE bounded away from zero as n grows, for any bandwidth including data-adaptive choices (Theorems 4.3–4.5, C.1–C.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolation with translation-invariant kernels is not benign (inconsistent) in fixed dimensions.

fits_no_version.finding: In Figure 6.1b, the exact expected error over Laplace-kernel bandwidth shows a trade-off between approximation error and noisy estimation error, with the optimum near M/N = 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kernel bandwidth trades approximation error against noise-fitting error in fixed-dimensional kernel interpolation.

record.peer_reviewed: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science
record.problems: The empirical illustration is a single one-dimensional target and kernel setting, and the plotted error values are not numerically tabulated in the text. The principal results are theoretical and rely on the stated fixed-design and spectral assumptions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional own results bearing on the specified versions were identified. Double-descent results in Related Work are cited results from other studies.

untested.parts: The theorems give an asymptotic lower bound only, not non-monotone error as n grows near a threshold.
Every estimator interpolates, so there is no risk-versus-capacity curve across the interpolation point.
No effective-complexity measure is used to predict peak location.
Noise and regularization are analyzed for consistency (Fig. 6.2), not for peak height, multiple peaks or peak removal.
No effective parameter count is used.

missing.what: Regularization illustration: a modified kernel that mimics ridge regularization, and KRR with λ=1 versus λ=0. Shown as predictor plots only, with no error values. A related, non-version result.

record.verdict_notes: Belkin is a co-author, but this paper is not one of the original sources. The d>1 torus results (Appendix C/D) extend r1–r3 and are not separately rowed, which is acceptable since they bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No deep-network model-size sweep or test-error curve.
The paper establishes non-vanishing error as sample size grows in its setting, but does not report that increasing sample size raises test error near an interpolation threshold.
No risk-versus-capacity curve across an interpolation point; inconsistency alone does not establish whether risk descends again.
No single effective-complexity measure is proposed or tested to predict peak locations.
The paper analyzes noise and regularization effects, but does not test whether they drive double-descent peaks, create multiple peaks, or eliminate peaks under optimally tuned regularization.
No comparison with an effective parameter count or test of whether such a count turns a second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: kernel interpolation (kernel ridgeless regression)
rows.operation_detail: Analyze expected generalization MSE as the grid resolution and sample count grow.

conditions.value: evenly spaced grid on the unit circle; n = N
fixed non-zero function with square-integrable zeroth and first derivatives and a convergent Fourier series

rows.value: Inconsistent: the expected MSE does not converge to zero as n grows.
rows.note: The theorem establishes non-vanishing error, not the shape of a test-error curve over model size, epochs, or sample size.

rows.subject: kernel interpolation (kernel ridgeless regression)
rows.operation_detail: Analyze consistency as the number of grid samples grows for a target constructed in the theorem.

conditions.value: evenly spaced grid on the unit circle; n = N
a function with constant H0-norm, whose existence is asserted

rows.value: Inconsistent for the constructed function for every bandwidth, including data-adaptive bandwidths.
rows.note: The result concerns consistency, not whether error rises or falls over a capacity sweep.

rows.subject: kernel interpolation (kernel ridgeless regression)
rows.operation_detail: Analyze consistency as the grid resolution and sample count grow, with bandwidth bounded by the resolution.

conditions.value: evenly spaced grid on the unit circle; n = N
any target with a convergent Fourier series

rows.value: Inconsistent for all stated targets; the noisy estimation error is bounded away from zero.
rows.locator: Theorem 4.5 and proof in Appendix A
rows.note: A positive lower bound does not specify a fall-rise-fall or monotone trend as sample size changes.

rows.subject: Laplace kernel interpolation
rows.operation_detail: Plot the exact-theory expected test error over a sweep of kernel bandwidth M.

conditions.value: M swept; the text says the optimal bandwidth is roughly M/N = 1

rows.measure: Expected average test MSE, with approximation and noisy estimation error also plotted
rows.note: The text describes a trade-off: larger bandwidth increases approximation error while allowing noise to be fit more benignly. Bandwidth is not one of the axes specified in the claim versions.
rows.check: The value is figure-only and the sweep is over bandwidth M at fixed N, with interpolation at every M. It is not a capacity sweep across an interpolation point, so no version's effect can be read from it. The row itself is correctly scoped.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
